## Goals

-   Fit models with more than one predictor (ANCOVA, interactions, two-way ANOVA)
-   Use `slopes`, `comparisons`, and `predictions` to interpret interactions
-   Report effects as estimates with confidence intervals

## Setup



::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
library(tidyverse)
library(marginaleffects)
```
:::



## ANCOVA: groups and a covariate

Using `iris`: does sepal length differ among species after accounting for petal length?



::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
ggplot(iris, aes(Petal.Length, Sepal.Length, color = Species)) +
  geom_point() +
  theme_minimal()
```

::: {.cell-output-display}
![Sepal vs. petal length by species](week10-tutorial_files/figure-html/fig-iris-1.png){#fig-iris width=672}
:::
:::

::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
m_anc <- lm(Sepal.Length ~ Species + Petal.Length, data = iris)
summary(m_anc)
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```

Call:
lm(formula = Sepal.Length ~ Species + Petal.Length, data = iris)

Residuals:
     Min       1Q   Median       3Q      Max 
-0.75310 -0.23142 -0.00081  0.23085  1.03100 

Coefficients:
                  Estimate Std. Error t value Pr(>|t|)    
(Intercept)        3.68353    0.10610  34.719  < 2e-16 ***
Speciesversicolor -1.60097    0.19347  -8.275 7.37e-14 ***
Speciesvirginica  -2.11767    0.27346  -7.744 1.48e-12 ***
Petal.Length       0.90456    0.06479  13.962  < 2e-16 ***
---
Signif. codes:  0 '***' 0.001 '**' 0.01 '*' 0.05 '.' 0.1 ' ' 1

Residual standard error: 0.338 on 146 degrees of freedom
Multiple R-squared:  0.8367,	Adjusted R-squared:  0.8334 
F-statistic: 249.4 on 3 and 146 DF,  p-value: < 2.2e-16
```


:::
:::



The model assumes the same slope in every species. `avg_comparisons()` reports species differences *adjusted* for petal length:



::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
avg_comparisons(m_anc, variables = list(Species = "pairwise"))
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```

    Term               Contrast Estimate Std. Error     z Pr(>|z|)    S  2.5 %
 Species versicolor - setosa      -1.601      0.193 -8.28   <0.001 52.8 -1.980
 Species virginica - setosa       -2.118      0.273 -7.74   <0.001 46.6 -2.654
 Species virginica - versicolor   -0.517      0.108 -4.80   <0.001 19.3 -0.728
 97.5 %
 -1.222
 -1.582
 -0.306

Columns: term, contrast, estimate, std.error, statistic, p.value, s.value, conf.low, conf.high 
Type:  response 
```


:::
:::



## Interactions: does the slope depend on species?



::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
m_int <- lm(Sepal.Length ~ Petal.Length * Species, data = iris)
summary(m_int)
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```

Call:
lm(formula = Sepal.Length ~ Petal.Length * Species, data = iris)

Residuals:
     Min       1Q   Median       3Q      Max 
-0.73479 -0.22785 -0.03132  0.24375  0.93608 

Coefficients:
                               Estimate Std. Error t value Pr(>|t|)    
(Intercept)                      4.2132     0.4074  10.341  < 2e-16 ***
Petal.Length                     0.5423     0.2768   1.959  0.05200 .  
Speciesversicolor               -1.8056     0.5984  -3.017  0.00302 ** 
Speciesvirginica                -3.1535     0.6341  -4.973 1.85e-06 ***
Petal.Length:Speciesversicolor   0.2860     0.2951   0.969  0.33405    
Petal.Length:Speciesvirginica    0.4534     0.2901   1.563  0.12029    
---
Signif. codes:  0 '***' 0.001 '**' 0.01 '*' 0.05 '.' 0.1 ' ' 1

Residual standard error: 0.3365 on 144 degrees of freedom
Multiple R-squared:  0.8405,	Adjusted R-squared:  0.8349 
F-statistic: 151.7 on 5 and 144 DF,  p-value: < 2.2e-16
```


:::

```{.r .cell-code}
anova(m_anc, m_int)
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```
Analysis of Variance Table

Model 1: Sepal.Length ~ Species + Petal.Length
Model 2: Sepal.Length ~ Petal.Length * Species
  Res.Df    RSS Df Sum of Sq      F Pr(>F)
1    146 16.682                           
2    144 16.301  2   0.38098 1.6828 0.1895
```


:::
:::



The coefficient table is hard to read: `Petal.Length` is the slope in the *reference* species only. Ask for the slope in each species instead:



::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
avg_slopes(m_int, variables = "Petal.Length", by = "Species")
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```

         Term    Contrast    Species Estimate Std. Error     z Pr(>|z|)    S
 Petal.Length mean(dY/dX) setosa        0.542     0.2767  1.96   0.0501  4.3
 Petal.Length mean(dY/dX) versicolor    0.828     0.1023  8.10   <0.001 50.7
 Petal.Length mean(dY/dX) virginica     0.996     0.0871 11.43   <0.001 98.2
     2.5 % 97.5 %
 -0.000122   1.08
  0.627797   1.03
  0.825064   1.17

Columns: term, contrast, Species, estimate, std.error, statistic, p.value, s.value, conf.low, conf.high, predicted_lo, predicted_hi, predicted 
Type:  response 
```


:::
:::



Is the slope for virginica different from versicolor?



::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
avg_slopes(m_int, variables = "Petal.Length", by = "Species", hypothesis = "pairwise")
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```

                   Term Estimate Std. Error      z Pr(>|z|)   S  2.5 % 97.5 %
 setosa - versicolor      -0.286      0.295 -0.969    0.332 1.6 -0.864 0.2923
 setosa - virginica       -0.453      0.290 -1.563    0.118 3.1 -1.022 0.1151
 versicolor - virginica   -0.167      0.134 -1.247    0.213 2.2 -0.431 0.0958

Columns: term, estimate, std.error, statistic, p.value, s.value, conf.low, conf.high 
Type:  response 
```


:::
:::

::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
plot_predictions(m_int, condition = c("Petal.Length", "Species")) +
  theme_minimal()
```

::: {.cell-output-display}
![Model predictions with an interaction](week10-tutorial_files/figure-html/fig-int-1.png){#fig-int width=672}
:::
:::

Why does the `setosa` slope have such a wide confidence interval? (Hint: look at the figure.)

## Two-way ANOVA: two factors

`ToothGrowth`: tooth length in guinea pigs by vitamin C supplement (`supp`) and dose.



::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
tg <- ToothGrowth |> mutate(dose = factor(dose))
m_tg <- lm(len ~ supp * dose, data = tg)
anova(m_tg)
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```
Analysis of Variance Table

Response: len
          Df  Sum Sq Mean Sq F value    Pr(>F)    
supp       1  205.35  205.35  15.572 0.0002312 ***
dose       2 2426.43 1213.22  92.000 < 2.2e-16 ***
supp:dose  2  108.32   54.16   4.107 0.0218603 *  
Residuals 54  712.11   13.19                      
---
Signif. codes:  0 '***' 0.001 '**' 0.01 '*' 0.05 '.' 0.1 ' ' 1
```


:::
:::



The interaction is significant, so "the effect of supplement" depends on dose. Estimate it at **each** dose:



::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
avg_comparisons(m_tg, variables = "supp", by = "dose")
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```

 Term            Contrast dose Estimate Std. Error       z Pr(>|z|)    S 2.5 %
 supp mean(VC) - mean(OJ)  0.5    -5.25       1.62 -3.2327  0.00123  9.7 -8.43
 supp mean(VC) - mean(OJ)  1      -5.93       1.62 -3.6514  < 0.001 11.9 -9.11
 supp mean(VC) - mean(OJ)  2       0.08       1.62  0.0493  0.96071  0.1 -3.10
 97.5 %
  -2.07
  -2.75
   3.26

Columns: term, contrast, dose, estimate, std.error, statistic, p.value, s.value, conf.low, conf.high, predicted_lo, predicted_hi, predicted 
Type:  response 
```


:::
:::

::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
avg_predictions(m_tg, by = c("supp", "dose"))
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```

 supp dose Estimate Std. Error     z Pr(>|z|)     S 2.5 % 97.5 %
   OJ  0.5    13.23       1.15 11.52   <0.001  99.6 10.98   15.5
   OJ  1      22.70       1.15 19.77   <0.001 286.5 20.45   25.0
   OJ  2      26.06       1.15 22.69   <0.001 376.3 23.81   28.3
   VC  0.5     7.98       1.15  6.95   <0.001  38.0  5.73   10.2
   VC  1      16.77       1.15 14.60   <0.001 158.0 14.52   19.0
   VC  2      26.14       1.15 22.76   <0.001 378.6 23.89   28.4

Columns: rowid, supp, dose, estimate, std.error, statistic, p.value, s.value, conf.low, conf.high, rowid_dedup 
Type:  response 
```


:::
:::

::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
plot_predictions(m_tg, condition = c("dose", "supp")) +
  theme_minimal()
```

::: {.cell-output-display}
![Predicted tooth length by supplement and dose](week10-tutorial_files/figure-html/fig-tg-1.png){#fig-tg width=672}
:::
:::



Is the supplement effect at dose 0.5 different from the effect at dose 2? That's a difference of differences:



::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
avg_comparisons(m_tg, variables = "supp", by = "dose", hypothesis = "b1 = b3")
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```

  Term Estimate Std. Error     z Pr(>|z|)   S 2.5 % 97.5 %
 b1=b3    -5.33        2.3 -2.32   0.0203 5.6 -9.83 -0.829

Columns: term, estimate, std.error, statistic, p.value, s.value, conf.low, conf.high 
Type:  response 
```


:::
:::



## Multiple regression with continuous predictors



::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
m_trees <- lm(Volume ~ Girth + Height, data = trees)
summary(m_trees)
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```

Call:
lm(formula = Volume ~ Girth + Height, data = trees)

Residuals:
    Min      1Q  Median      3Q     Max 
-6.4065 -2.6493 -0.2876  2.2003  8.4847 

Coefficients:
            Estimate Std. Error t value Pr(>|t|)    
(Intercept) -57.9877     8.6382  -6.713 2.75e-07 ***
Girth         4.7082     0.2643  17.816  < 2e-16 ***
Height        0.3393     0.1302   2.607   0.0145 *  
---
Signif. codes:  0 '***' 0.001 '**' 0.01 '*' 0.05 '.' 0.1 ' ' 1

Residual standard error: 3.882 on 28 degrees of freedom
Multiple R-squared:  0.948,	Adjusted R-squared:  0.9442 
F-statistic:   255 on 2 and 28 DF,  p-value: < 2.2e-16
```


:::
:::

::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
avg_slopes(m_trees)
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```

   Term Estimate Std. Error     z Pr(>|z|)     S  2.5 % 97.5 %
 Girth     4.708      0.264 17.82  < 0.001 233.4 4.1902  5.226
 Height    0.339      0.130  2.61  0.00914   6.8 0.0842  0.594

Columns: term, estimate, std.error, statistic, p.value, s.value, conf.low, conf.high 
Type:  response 
```


:::
:::



Compare the `Height` slope here with last week's `Volume ~ Height` model. What changed, and why?



::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
cor(trees$Girth, trees$Height)
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```
[1] 0.5192801
```


:::

Use `plot_slopes(m_trees, variables = "Height", condition = "Girth")` to see how the Height slope changes with Girth. Is it constant? Why should it be, in this model?
:::

## Design reminder

::: callout-important
## Randomization and covariates

ANCOVA's strength in experiments is **precision**: if treatment was randomly assigned, adjusting for a baseline covariate leaves the treatment estimate unbiased and shrinks its standard error. In observational data, adjustment cannot rescue a confounded design.
:::
